Before I write it up, one bigger choice needs your decision. The answer changes most of what gets built.

This is a project, not a small change. I'll write a full design document and save it with the website code. You review it there. A fresh session then plans the build from it.

The open choice is how volunteers get a recording from their phone into the guide. Your website is made of fixed pages that are rebuilt and published on each change. It has no place to receive uploads yet. I see two sensible ways:

1. **Upload page with separate audio storage (recommended).** A volunteer signs in to a simple page on their phone. They pick the exhibit and the language, then upload the recording. The guide cleans the audio and stores it outside the website code. It goes live with no site rebuild. The cost is a small server-side part and a volunteer sign-in to look after.
2. **Edit through a content editor on the website.** A ready-made editing tool adds an admin area to the site. Each upload is saved with the website files and triggers a rebuild, and the cleanup runs during that rebuild. There is less new code. But these editors are awkward on a phone. The audio files also grow the website code by a few hundred megabytes over the years.

I dropped a paid audio-guide service. It moves the stories off your site, and most of these services do not clean the audio automatically.

I recommend option 1. Volunteers record on phones, so uploading from the phone has to be easy.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The site is built by Eleventy and hosted on Netlify. Every page is generated ahead of time, so nothing on it can accept a file today.
- Netlify can run small server-side functions next to a static site. Option 1 relies on that to receive uploads and clean the audio.
- Option 2 stores audio in the same place as the website code. Audio is large and changes often, and that kind of storage handles it badly.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

Which way do you want to go?
